concepts.unsupported: Not tied to any part of the brief — check the idea, or the brief.
concepts.briefEmpty: This brief has nothing written in it yet, so there is nothing to propose against.
concepts.nothingRemoved: Nothing has been removed from the concept, so there is nothing to regenerate. Delete an item first.
concepts.failed: The concept could not be proposed right now. The brief is unaffected — try again in a moment.
concepts.markFailed: That change could not be saved. Reload the page to see the concept as it stands.
concepts.discardFailed: The concept could not be discarded. Try again.
concepts.loadFailed: The proposed concept could not be loaded.

requirements.cycle: That would make two tasks wait on each other. Pick a different one.
requirements.addFailed: The requirement could not be added. Nothing was changed — try again, or report this.
requirements.externalIntro: Things this deliverable needs from a client or a supplier. Every task under it shows what is outstanding, and the clock on each one starts when it is asked for.
requirements.addInput: Add something we are waiting for
requirements.descriptionHint: What exactly? e.g. Acme logo pack

briefApproval.pending: This department has not approved its brief yet, so none of its work can be assigned.
briefApproval.locked: locked — re-open it to make a change
briefApproval.reopenMessage: The approval is withdrawn so the brief can be edited. Until it is approved again, none of this department's work can be newly assigned. The re-opening is recorded with your name.
briefApproval.reopenOutsideScope: Only this department's lead, the account manager or Traffic can re-open its brief.
briefApproval.outsideScope: You cannot approve this department's brief. Its own lead can, and so can Traffic or a Power Admin.
briefApproval.failed: The brief's approval could not be saved. It is unchanged — try again, or report this.

deadlineExtension.askIntro: The committed deadline is {{date}}. Asking changes nothing until {{approver}} answers; work carries on meanwhile.
deadlineExtension.askIntroNoApprover: The committed deadline is {{date}}. Asking changes nothing until it is answered; work carries on meanwhile.
deadlineExtension.askIntroUndated: There is no committed date yet. Asking changes nothing until {{approver}} answers; work carries on meanwhile.
deadlineExtension.askIntroUndatedNoApprover: There is no committed date yet. Asking changes nothing until it is answered; work carries on meanwhile.
deadlineExtension.planPastCommitment: The plan now ends on {{plan}}, after the committed deadline of {{committed}}.
deadlineExtension.offerFromMove: The dates you saved end after the committed deadline. Ask for an extension to {{date}}?
deadlineExtension.reasonHint: One line — this is the message the approver decides on.
deadlineExtension.attribution_dependency: An input — waiting on something else
deadlineExtension.pendingLineNoApprover: Extension requested to {{date}}, awaiting an answer
deadlineExtension.arithmetic_fine: Leaves {{days}} working days before the deliverable is due, with {{buffer}} needed for review — fine.
deadlineExtension.arithmetic_tight: Leaves {{days}} working days before the deliverable is due, exactly the {{buffer}} needed for review — tight.
deadlineExtension.arithmetic_at_risk: Leaves {{days}} working days before the deliverable is due, less than the {{buffer}} needed for review — the deliverable is at risk. The account manager may still approve, and then renegotiates with the client.
deadlineExtension.arithmetic_after_go_live: That date is after the campaign goes live. It can be asked for, but the account manager will need the client's agreement before approving it.
deadlineExtension.arithmetic_past_due: This is {{days}} working days past the deliverable's own due date — the account manager will need to approve it, and may need the client's agreement.
deadlineExtension.arithmetic_none: This deliverable has no promised date to measure against.
deadlineExtension.refused: You cannot do that here. The assignee, or somebody who can reschedule the task, may ask; the campaign's account manager answers.
deadlineExtension.failed: The extension could not be saved. Nothing was changed — try again, or report this.
deadlineExtension.changePromiseIntro: The client has agreed to a new date for “{{name}}”. Attach their agreement — an email or a screenshot — and it is filed in this campaign's References.
deadlineExtension.evidenceOptional: Attach the client's agreement if you have it — the change is logged either way.
deadlineExtension.evidenceFailed: The attachment could not be filed. Try again.
deadlineExtension.noReferencesFolder: This campaign has no References folder to file the agreement in.
deadlineExtension.changePromiseRefused: Only the campaign's account manager can change the promised date.

intake.title: New single job
intake.intro: One request, one deliverable, one department. The clock starts when the client asked — not now.

briefType.title: What are we making?
briefType.intro: Say who it is for, then pick the kind of brief. The questions, the fields and the team all change to suit it.
briefType.inheritsBrand: The {{brand}} library and its folders come with this choice.
briefType.inheritsClient: {{client}}'s library and folders come with this choice. Pick a brand to narrow it.
briefType.inheritsNone: Pick a client and the brief takes on their library.
briefType.noTemplates: No brief template has any fields yet. An administrator adds them under Admin → Brief templates.
briefType.noMatch: Nothing matches “{{query}}”. Clear the search to see every brief.
briefType.campaignInstead: More than one deliverable? Start a campaign instead
briefType.inheritsLine_one: {{count}} dos-and-don’ts rule and the {{library}} library come with this choice.
briefType.inheritsLine_other: {{count}} dos-and-don’ts rules and the {{library}} library come with this choice.

door.title: What are you bringing in?
door.intro: Everything starts here. A single job is one deliverable for one department; a campaign is a plan across several.
door.singleJobText: One request, one deliverable, one department. Capture who asked and what they asked for, write the brief, release it to the department lead.
door.fullCampaignText: Strategy, several deliverables across departments, timing and review. Opens the campaign builder.
door.shortcutHint: {{keys}} opens this from anywhere. Escape closes it.
door.promoteNote: A single job can be promoted to a campaign later, without retyping.

noAccess.title: Projects are created by an account manager
noAccess.body: Ask an Account Manager to create the project for you — or, if it is an internal project, request the required permissions.

clock.notStarted: The clock has not started — confirm when the request arrived on the proof below.

request.saving: Saving the request and filing the evidence…
request.title: Job title
request.titleHint: What the job is called on every list. It must be unique for this client.
request.clientLocked: The job is filed under this client now. To change the client, cancel and start again.
request.askedByHint: A name — a client contact, or somebody down the corridor.
request.words: What they asked for, in their words
request.wordsHint: Their words, not your summary. This is the line everyone reads back later.
request.typeHint: Type to search the deliverable types…
request.typeNone: No type yet. Without one, no task list is generated — the department lead breaks the work down by hand.
request.quantityHint: Three statics are one deliverable whose creation step becomes three tasks.
request.dueHint: Typed, not proposed: no deliverable type carries a lead time yet, so any suggestion would be invented.
request.departmentHint: The department's lead becomes the owner and picks who does the work.
request.noLead: {{department}} has no department lead set up. The job will have no owner until one is named on the deliverable — and nobody can approve its task list until then.
request.noLeadPickTeamLead: {{department}} has no department lead yet — name a team lead as the owner. Pick one where there is more than one.
request.loadWeekDue: {{department}} is at {{pct}}% for the week it is due ({{week}})
request.loadNone: Nobody in {{department}} has a calendar yet.
request.moreNote: More than one deliverable? Open the campaign builder.

brief.heading: What {{department}} needs to know
brief.intro: Six fields, empty, with their guidance. Write them from the request above. Nothing is prefilled from the client — the details belong to this job, not to them.
brief.riskHint: A reminder for the department lead, who attaches it to the right task when they review the list. Nothing waits on this text.
brief.attachmentsHint: Reference material, not proof. The proof is the receipt on the previous screen; this is everything else, filed into the job's References.
brief.unreviewed: {{n}} field(s) filled from the brief — review or edit each, then click ‘Keep’.
brief.reviewBlocked: All brief fields must be confirmed by clicking ‘Keep’ in order to progress to review.
brief.onePage: One page. Nothing is prefilled — the details belong to this job, not to the client. Autosaved.
brief.onePagePrefilled: One page. The document has filled what it could; the rest is yours. Autosaved.
brief.rulesNone: Nothing travels with this deliverable yet — {{client}} has no dos and don’ts on its profile. Add them under Clients and they appear here, locked.
brief.attachmentsSoon: Attachments file into the job's References once the job exists — one step back, then Next.
brief.riskWho: a reminder for the department lead
brief.notUsedThis: {{client}} has not had this kind of brief before.
brief.rulesFrom: From {{from}}. They travel with this deliverable; you cannot edit them here.

review.proofNone: No proof yet. The clock has not started; the job can still be released.
review.proofNoneClockStarted: No screenshot filed — the arrival was recorded by hand, so the clock has already started.
review.landsWith: {{department}}. {{owner}} is the lead. It lands in their queue the moment you approve; they review the task list and pick who does it.
review.landsNoOwner: {{department}}, which has no lead yet. The job will wait until an owner is named on the deliverable.
review.whatApproveDoes: Approve releases the job: the brief is approved with it, the task list is generated and held for the lead's review, and nobody is assigned anything until the lead approves that list.
review.tracked: After you approve, changes are tracked and the lead sees them.
review.footNote: Opening the job sends it to the owner and starts their clock.
review.title: Read it once, then open it
review.subtitle: Exactly as it will land on {{department}}’s desk.
review.subtitleNamed: Exactly as it will land on {{owner}}’s desk.
review.rulesNone: None on file for {{client}} yet — add dos and don’ts to the client profile and they travel with every deliverable.
review.footNoteNamed: Opening sends it to {{owner}} and starts their clock.
review.rulesFrom_one: From {{from}}. {{count}} rule travels with every deliverable.
review.rulesFrom_other: From {{from}}. {{count}} rules travel with every deliverable.

similar.title: {{client}} already has a job that looks like this
similar.intro: “{{name}}” was raised {{when}} by {{who}}, and it is still with {{department}}. Two jobs for the same asset means two briefs, two clocks and one confused designer.
similar.why: Adding it as a second deliverable keeps one brief, one clock and one conversation with {{who}}.
similar.whyNoOne: Adding it as a second deliverable keeps one brief, one clock and one conversation.
similar.openIt: Open it in a new tab

cancel.title: Leave without releasing?
cancel.message: The job already exists — the proof and attachments were filed into it. Leaving does not release it.
cancel.stays: It stays under Drafts on the campaigns list, where it can be continued or discarded.
cancel.nothingAssigned: Nobody is assigned anything until it is approved.

errors.incomplete: Fill in the fields marked * before moving on.
errors.incompleteList: Fill in these required fields before moving on: {{fields}}.
errors.ownerRequired: Name a team lead as the owner before releasing — this department has no lead.
errors.saveFailed: The request could not be saved. Nothing was lost on screen — try again, or report this.
errors.similarFailed: The job was released, but the check for similar open jobs could not run. If this might be a duplicate, look for it on the campaigns list.
errors.approveScope: You cannot approve this job: it is outside your reach. Its account manager can.
errors.approveScopeNamed: Only this client's account manager, {{name}}, can approve this job. It is saved for them — they will find it on the campaigns list.
errors.approveScopeNoManager: This client has no account manager, so nobody can approve this job yet. Set one on the client record, then approve. The job is saved.
errors.attachFailed: The job could not be attached. Nothing was changed — try again, or keep them separate.
errors.jobNotFound: That job could not be found.
errors.noTemplate: The Single Execution brief template is not set up for this tenant. The brief screen will have no fields until an administrator adds it under Admin → Brief templates.
errors.alreadyReleased: This job has already been released. Open it to see where it is.
errors.fieldRequired: “{{field}}” is the one field this brief cannot go without.
errors.alreadySent: This job has already been sent for approval, so it can no longer be changed here. It is waiting for its approver — open it from Campaigns.

wizard.notDraft: This is no longer a draft, so the builder cannot pick it up here. Open it from the campaigns list instead.
wizard.sentWaiting: This job has already been sent for approval — it is waiting for {{name}}. Nothing here can be changed; Open releases it if you are its approver.

schedule.projectOnly: Pick a task from a project. A new job or campaign starts at the front door (Ctrl/Cmd P), not here.

promote.title: Turn this job into a campaign?
promote.message: {{name}} becomes a campaign and opens as one, with what you already have kept; departments and deliverables are added there.
promote.keeps: Kept as they are: the client and brand, the proof and its clock, the brief, the deliverable and its owner.
promote.oneWay: This cannot be undone. A campaign that has gained a strategy and other departments has no honest way back to one deliverable for one department.
promote.failed: The job could not be promoted. Nothing was changed.
promote.comes2: The proof and its clock — the original start
promote.adds4: Each department's own brief and approval
promote.adds5: A campaign-level view the client can see
promote.keepSingle: Keep it as a single job
promote.note: This cannot be undone once approved.

held.approveWhat: The generated list is a proposal until you say so. Approving opens it for assignment; you can still add, remove and reorder tasks afterwards.
held.risk: What could stop this (from the request):
held.riskHint: A reminder from the account manager. Attach the real dependency to the right task below — nothing waits on this text.
held.approveFailed: The list could not be approved. Its owner can, and so can anyone who may change the owner.

who.title: Who makes it, and when do they need it by?
who.intro: Pick the department. The lead decides who.
who.landsInQueue: It lands in their queue the moment you open the job. They pick who does it.
who.neverAPerson: Assign the deliverable’s owner. If the lead has not assigned it within {{hours}} hours it escalates to the traffic manager on its own.
who.countedBack: Maestro counted it back for you
who.weekNote: Sunday to Thursday — Friday and Saturday are not counted.
who.neverAPersonNamed: Assign the deliverable’s owner. If {{lead}} has not assigned it within {{hours}} hours it escalates to the traffic manager on its own.

suggestion.asking: Reading the brief for what it asks to be made…
suggestion.suggested: Suggested from the brief — change anything that is wrong.
suggestion.none: The brief did not name anything to make. Choose it below.
suggestion.failed: The brief could not be read for suggestions just now. Choose below — nothing is lost.

who.campaignWarning: This reads like a campaign rather than a single job.
who.campaignWarningDepartments: Its deliverables belong to more than one department.
who.campaignWarningDates: Its deliverables are due on different days.

short.title: {{day}} is {{n}} days short
short.intro: A {{type}} needs {{needs}} working days and you have given it {{has}}. Nothing stops — it goes out tagged Reduced scope, and the tag is recorded on the job.
short.introUntyped: This job needs {{needs}} working days and you have given it {{has}}. Nothing stops — it goes out tagged Reduced scope, and the tag is recorded on the job.
short.means1: One round of changes, not two.
short.means2: No extra language adaptation in this timeframe.
short.means3: The lead picks whoever is free, not whoever is right.
short.note: The tag is recorded on the job. When the date moves later, this is what the conversation refers back to.

refusals.askNobody: Ask your department lead or Traffic.
refusals.reorder_tasks: You cannot reorder this list: it is outside your reach.
refusals.remove_task: You cannot remove this task: it is outside your reach.
refusals.cancel_task: You cannot cancel this task: it is outside your reach.
refusals.reinstate_task: You cannot reinstate this task: it is outside your reach.
refusals.create_adhoc: You cannot give this person work: they are outside your reach.
refusals.approve_brief: You cannot approve this department's brief: it is outside your reach.
refusals.reopen_brief: You cannot re-open this department's brief: it is outside your reach.
refusals.promote_job: You cannot promote this job to a campaign: it is outside your reach.
refusals.attach_job: You cannot attach this job to that campaign: one of them is outside your reach.

edit.title: Task
edit.notesHint: Anything relevant to this task — whoever does it reads this.

taskLists.heading: Task lists to approve
taskLists.intro: Work cannot be handed out until the person who owns it has read its task list and accepted it.

workstreams.heading: Workstreams
workstreams.noneYet: This campaign is not grouped into workstreams. It does not have to be.
workstreams.name: Name
workstreams.removeEmpty: It holds no work, so nothing is lost.
workstreams.cannotRemove: "{{name}}" still holds {{count}} deliverables. Move them out or remove them first.
workstreams.changingDepartmentMovesWork: Changing the department will move the {{count}} deliverables in this workstream, and their unassigned tasks, to it.

work.title: What are we actually making?
work.lede: Add a workstream, then list the deliverables under it like bullet points. Most campaigns are one or two workstreams.
work.hint: Each line becomes a deliverable with the workstream's department. Format and phase are guessed from the words and fixed in Details. Enter adds the next line.
work.newGroupHint: — a name and a department. Most campaigns need one or two.
work.summary: {{pieces}} deliverables across {{groups}} workstreams. Every one gets its own clock when the campaign is approved.

piece.addLede: It takes the workstream's department and manager. You say what it is and when.
piece.editLede: Before the campaign is approved, any change is just an edit. After, it becomes a change request the team lead has to accept.
piece.name: Deliverable
piece.ideaHint: The line the creative reads first.
piece.severalLanguages: Each language becomes its own deliverable, so it can have its own owner and its own status. {{count}} deliverables will be created.
piece.typeHint: Brings its own task list and its own lead time.
piece.quantityHint: Three sizes of one visual is one deliverable, three of them.
piece.channelHint: The platform it goes out on.
piece.notesHint: Anything the team should know that does not fit above. Optional.
piece.addLedeLoose: You say what it is, who owns it and when. Its department comes from its owner.

removePiece.title: Remove {{name}}?
removePiece.ledeClean: Nobody has started it, so this is clean. It comes off the season map and the grid, and its slot is freed.
removePiece.ledeStarted: Somebody is already on this one. Removing it takes it off the grid, and the hours already spent stay on the record.
removePiece.noteHead: If work had started, this would be a change request instead
removePiece.noteBody: A deliverable somebody is already on cannot just vanish. The team lead has to accept it, and the hours already spent stay on the record.
removePiece.restorable: Restorable from the campaign record for 30 days.

newWorkstream.title: New workstream
newWorkstream.lede: A name and the department it goes to. That is all a workstream needs. The deliverables come next, as a list under it.
newWorkstream.name: Name
newWorkstream.nameTaken: This campaign already has a workstream called "{{name}}".
newWorkstream.lettersHint: Its deliverables are coded {{example}}. Fixed once it is made.
newWorkstream.lettersInvalid: Two to four letters, A to Z.
newWorkstream.renameLede: The name only. The workstream keeps its department, and each deliverable stays with its owner’s.

brief.title: The campaign brief
brief.lede: The Creative Brief, in five parts. Long briefs are one page you scroll, not seventeen screens. Short ones stay one question at a time.

drop.title: Got a brief already? Drop it here
drop.hint: Word, text or Markdown. Maestro fills the fields below for you to fix — it never sends anything you did not read.

brief.lockedRule: The client's rule. It cannot be cancelled here.
brief.budgetNote: Budget is on the template and not shown.

rule.title: Add a do or a don't
rule.intro: It travels with every deliverable in this campaign. A campaign rule can sit on top of the client's; it can never cancel one.
rule.textPlaceholder: What to always do, or never do.
rule.becausePlaceholder: Who asked for it, and when.
rule.becauseHint: optional, but the next person will thank you
rule.lockedNote: The client's rules stay locked underneath. Anyone reviewing a deliverable sees both lists, and the source of each.

timing.title: Every phase plans back from its own end date
timing.lede: Maestro has already counted everything back. Here you change a phase's dates, give a deliverable a date of its own, mark a date as given to the client, and see what will not fit.

givenToClient.title: Mark a date as given to the client
givenToClient.body: A marker on the deliverable: the client has been told this date.

willNotFit.title: See what will not fit
willNotFit.body: Amber rows are short of their lead time. They go out as reduced scope, with the client's sign-off recorded.

editPhase.title: Edit a phase
editPhase.body: Press the pencil on the strip. Every deliverable in the phase re-plans from its new end date.

editPiece.title: Give a deliverable its own date
editPiece.body: Press Edit on the row. A date in another phase — earlier or later — moves the deliverable into that phase.

editPiecePlain.title: Set each deliverable's date
editPiecePlain.body: Press Edit on the row. Maestro counts the start back from the date, over working days only.

goLive.title: Set the go-live, if there is one
goLive.body: Optional. Dates still blank are filled back from it; dates already set are left alone.

timing.workingWeekMixed: WORKING WEEK — SEE THE OFFICE CALENDAR
timing.noPieces: Nothing is in this phase yet. Add deliverables on the work step.
timing.footnote: Fridays and Saturdays are never counted. Edit a deliverable to give it a date of its own — a date in another phase moves it there.
timing.broughtBack: BROUGHT BACK TO THE PHASE END

addPhase.title: Add a phase
addPhase.intro: A phase runs from its start date to its end date. Everything in it plans back from the end date.
addPhase.name: Name
addPhase.beforeStart: A phase cannot end before it starts on {{day}}.
addPhase.note: No deliverables are created by adding a phase. Add them on the work step as you need them.
addPhase.footnote: The phase appears on the season strip straight away.
addPhase.startsAfterHint: Filled in as the day after {{phase}} ends. Change it if there is a gap.

editPhase.title: Edit the phase
editPhase.overlapsBefore: It starts before {{phase}} ends on {{day}}. Start it after that, or edit {{phase}} first.
editPhase.passesAfter: {{phase}} ends on {{day}}. End this one before that, or edit {{phase}} first.
editPhase.pushesNext: {{phase}} will now start on {{day}}, so the two do not overlap.
editPhase.pieceMoves: {{piece}} moves to {{phase}} — its own date, {{day}}, falls there now.

timing.notInAPhase_one: One deliverable is not in a phase yet, so it has no date. Edit it to give it one.
timing.notInAPhase_other: {{count}} deliverables are not in a phase yet, so they have no dates. Edit each to give it one.

pieceDialog.outside: That day is outside every phase. The phases run: {{ranges}}.
pieceDialog.notWorking: {{typed}} is not a working day, so it is due {{day}}.
pieceDialog.starts_one: Work starts {{day}} — {{count}} working day, counting the day it is due.
pieceDialog.starts_other: Work starts {{day}} — {{count}} working days, counting the day it is due.
pieceDialog.given: The client has been given this date
pieceDialog.givenTip: A marker only. It records that the client has been told this date; it adds no second date and blocks nothing.

plain.title: When each deliverable is due
plain.lede: This campaign has no phases, so each deliverable has a date of its own. Maestro counts the start back from it, over working days only.
plain.goLiveTip: Setting it fills every blank date: delivery {{delivery}} working days before it, work starting {{commence}} working days before that. Dates already set are left alone. A date too close to go-live, or after it, warns and is allowed.
plain.heading: The deliverables
plain.empty: No deliverables yet. Add them on the work step.
plain.footnote: Fridays and Saturdays are never counted. A deliverable with no date cannot leave this step.

approve.title: This one is yours to approve
approve.lede: You are the account manager on {{client}}. Approving starts the clocks and sends the work to its owners.
approve.noDirector: There is no second signature to wait for. This one is yours.

does.leads_one: {{count}} lead gets their workstream in their queue
does.leads_other: {{count}} leads get their workstream in their queue
does.grid: Every deliverable appears on the grid, on its planned days
does.library: The campaign's folders are filed under {{path}}
does.escalation_one: Work nobody has picked up is chased after {{count}} hour
does.escalation_other: Work nobody has picked up is chased after {{count}} hours
does.owners_one: {{count}} owner is told the work is theirs, and approves its task list before anyone is assigned
does.owners_other: {{count}} owners are told the work is theirs, and each approves their task lists before anyone is assigned

approve.notReadyBody: Save it as a draft. Nothing is told to anybody, no clock starts, and it is waiting exactly as you left it.
approve.onTheRecord: Your name and the time go on the campaign record.
approve.notYours: {{name}} approves this campaign. Ask them to open it.
approve.noSummary: No proposition written yet — edit the brief to add one.

phasesPanel.title: Phases
phasesPanel.aside: each ends on its own date
phasesPanel.explain: A phase is a stretch of the campaign with its own start and end date. Every deliverable inside it plans back from the phase’s end date.
phasesPanel.offBody: This campaign runs straight through. Every deliverable plans back from its own due date, and nothing is grouped into stretches.

moveWorkstream.title: Move {{name}}
moveWorkstream.intro: A workstream is what sets a deliverable's department, so moving it is not just tidying. Pick where it belongs.
moveWorkstream.noneLine: It stays in the campaign and keeps the department it has.
moveWorkstream.changesDepartment: This moves it from {{from}} to {{to}}. Tasks nobody has started follow it; anything already picked up stays where it is.
moveWorkstream.outKeepsDepartment: Taking it out changes the grouping and nothing else. It keeps its department.
moveWorkstream.footnote: The people who lose it and the people who gain it are both told.

proposal.title: Here is what the brief suggests we make
proposal.lede: Read from the brief you just wrote. Nothing here exists until you keep it. Drop what is wrong, edit what is close, add what is missing.
proposal.ownerTip: The person who answers for this workstream: a department lead, a team lead or a deputy team lead. It can be changed at any time.
proposal.needsWorkstream: Not in a workstream — move each one into a workstream
proposal.groupEmpty: Nothing in this workstream yet — press Add.
proposal.newWorkstreamHint: — for anything the brief did not suggest.
proposal.summary: {{kept}} kept, {{dropped}} dropped. Dropped deliverables go when you move on to timing. Nothing is booked and nobody is told until the campaign is approved.
proposal.missingDepartment: Give each workstream a department before moving on: {{names}}.
proposal.none: The brief did not suggest anything to make. Add workstreams and deliverables yourself.
proposal.quickAdd: Add a deliverable — Enter for the next
proposal.workLede: Add a workstream, then list the deliverables under it like bullet points. Most campaigns are one or two workstreams.

workstreamsSwitch.title: Workstreams
workstreamsSwitch.toggleLabel: Group this campaign's work into workstreams
workstreamsSwitch.onBody: The brief's deliverables arrive grouped into workstreams, each with a department and an owner.
workstreamsSwitch.offBody: The work is one list. Each deliverable's department comes from its owner.
workstreamsSwitch.refused_one: {{count}} deliverable is in a workstream. Move it out on The work before switching this off.
workstreamsSwitch.refused_other: {{count}} deliverables are in workstreams. Move them out on The work before switching this off.

reopen.title: Re-open {{name}}
reopen.intro: Tick what needs doing again. Each task goes back to To do with nobody on it, to be assigned again on the Schedule; its reviewers stay. The rest stay approved.
reopen.tasksHint: At least one. Only approved tasks are offered.
reopen.noneFinished: Nothing here is approved yet, so there is nothing to re-open.
reopen.reasonHint: It goes on the record and to everyone told — the reviewers and the owner.
reopen.dueHint: The re-opened work's new commitment. Due at 18:00 Iraq time that day.
reopen.consequence_one: 1 task goes back to To do. If the campaign was closed, it opens again.
reopen.consequence_other: {{count}} tasks go back to To do. If the campaign was closed, it opens again.
